newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares continue strong in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares continue strong in quiet trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares continued largely strong in quiet Monday trade with brokers saying their two-week bull-run was beginning to tail off and the bourse would be looking for new direction.
The key industrial index put on 6.09 points to end at a record peak of 8,051.84.

"The market is looking strong but it is letting off steam a bit. It will definitely be looking for new direction soon. Good rains will be a pointer and also the IMF (International Monetary Fund)'s position on new funding for ZIMPREST," one broker said.

The government of President Robert Mugabe is due to start negotiations this month with the IMF on new donor funding for a second tranche of its second economic reform programme called the Zimbabwe Programme for Economic and Social Transformation (ZIMPREST).

On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Monday, rubber and agricultural manufacturer Acacia rose 10 cents to 270 while seed producer and distributor Seedco and packaging firm Hunyani added five cents each to 195 and 345 respectively and tea and coffee company EHPL firmed two cents to 147.
Against the trend, publishing group Zimpapers dropped 50 cents to 2,050, battery manufacturer Chloride lost five cents to 80 and tissue mill KCI eased three cents to 45.
Minings were quiet with nickel producer Bindura unchanged at 1,050 while Mhangura copper mine added five cents to 30 as did Wankie Colliery to 365.
The mining index edged 2.55 points up to 1,232.88.
